Thyroid Eye Disease (TED), also known as Graves’ orbitopathy, is a complex condition that affects the tissues around the eyes, causing inflammation, swelling, and discomfort. At AestheticEye, our top oculoplastic surgeons in Cincinnati, Dr. Ginger Henson and Dr. Jonathan Pargament, specialize in the diagnosis and surgical treatment of TED. Our team is committed to providing advanced, personalized care to help you manage this condition and restore your eye health and appearance.

What is Thyroid Eye Disease?

Thyroid Eye Disease is an autoimmune disorder often associated with hyperthyroidism, where the body’s immune system attacks the tissues around the eyes. This results in inflammation and swelling, leading to a range of symptoms that can significantly impact your quality of life.

Symptoms of Thyroid Eye Disease

Common symptoms of TED include:

Proptosis (Bulging Eyes)

Eyes that appear to protrude from the eye sockets.

Eyelid Retraction

Eyelids that are pulled back, exposing more of the eye.

Double Vision

: Seeing double due to misalignment of the eyes.

Eye Pain and Discomfort

Persistent pain or discomfort around the eyes.

Dryness and Redness

Irritation and dryness caused by the exposure of the eye surface.

Vision Problems

Blurred vision or vision loss in severe cases.

Causes and Risk Factors of TED

Thyroid Eye Disease is most commonly associated with Graves’ disease, an autoimmune condition that affects the thyroid gland. Risk factors for TED include:

Hyperthyroidism

Overactive thyroid gland.

Smoking

Increases the severity of TED.

Gender

Women are more commonly affected than men.

Genetic Factors

Family history of thyroid or autoimmune diseases.

Advanced Surgical Solutions for Thyroid Eye Disease

The surgical treatment of Thyroid Eye Disease aims to relieve symptoms, restore normal eye appearance, and improve eye function. At AestheticEye, we offer a range of advanced surgical solutions tailored to each patient’s specific needs.

Orbital Decompression Surgery

Orbital decompression surgery is performed to create more space within the orbit, reducing pressure on the eye and allowing it to move back into a more natural position.

The Procedure

Bone Removal

Removing or reshaping parts of the orbital bones to create additional space.

Fat Removal

In some cases, excess fat is removed to further reduce pressure.

Eyelid Surgery

Eyelid surgery addresses issues such as eyelid retraction and proptosis, helping to protect the eyes and restore a more natural appearance.

Types of Eyelid Surgery

Eyelid Retraction Repair

Repositioning the eyelids to cover the eye adequately and reduce exposure.

Blepharoplasty

Removing excess skin and fat to improve eyelid function and appearance.

Strabismus Surgery

Strabismus surgery corrects double vision by realigning the eye muscles, ensuring that the eyes move together properly.

The Procedure

Muscle Realignment

Adjusting the muscles around the eye to improve alignment and reduce double vision.

Frequently Asked Questions | Thyroid Eye Disease Treatment

What Are the First Signs of Thyroid Eye Disease?

The initial signs of TED often include redness, swelling, and discomfort around the eyes. Patients may also notice bulging eyes and eyelid retraction.

How Long Does It Take to Recover from Orbital Decompression Surgery?

Recovery time varies, but most patients experience significant improvement within a few weeks. Full recovery may take several months, with regular follow-up appointments to monitor progress.

Can Thyroid Eye Disease Be Treated Without Surgery?

Mild cases of TED can often be managed with medications and lifestyle changes, such as quitting smoking. However, severe cases typically require surgical intervention for optimal outcomes.

Will My Vision Improve After Surgery for Thyroid Eye Disease?

Surgical treatment aims to alleviate symptoms and improve eye function. Many patients experience significant improvement in vision and relief from discomfort after surgery.

Are There Risks Associated with Surgical Treatment for TED?

As with any surgery, there are potential risks, including infection, bleeding, and complications related to anesthesia. These risks are minimized when the surgery is performed by experienced oculoplastic surgeons like Dr. Henson and Dr. Pargament.

How Do I Know If I Am a Candidate for Surgery?

If you are experiencing severe symptoms of TED that do not respond to medical treatment, you may be a candidate for surgery. A comprehensive evaluation by our surgeons will determine the best course of action for your specific condition.
